question: Who among the following is the founder of the Vrindavan Gurukul in Mumbai and Vrindavan Gurukul in Bhubaneshwar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Hariprasad Chaurasia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Hariprasad Chaurasia**, a renowned Indian flutist, is credited with establishing the Vrindavan Gurukul in Mumbai and Bhubaneshwar.
 
• The Vrindavan Gurukul is a center dedicated to teaching and preserving the art of Indian classical music, especially the **bansuri (bamboo flute)**.
 
• Hariprasad Chaurasia follows the **Guru-Shishya Parampara** (teacher-student tradition) at the Gurukul, where students live and learn under his guidance.
 
• The Gurukuls were set up to provide a serene environment for learning Indian classical music away from urban distractions.
 
• Both Mumbai and Bhubaneshwar centers are known for nurturing talented musicians and preserving India's rich musical heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hariprasad Chaurasia**

 
 
• He is one of the most celebrated flutists in Indian classical music and a recipient of numerous awards, including the **Padma Bhushan (1992)** and **Padma Vibhushan (2000)**.
 
• His music is rooted in the **Hindustani classical tradition**, and he is known for his unique playing style.
 
• Hariprasad Chaurasia has collaborated with international artists and contributed to globalizing Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Guru-Shishya Parampara**
 
 
• This is an ancient Indian tradition of teaching where students (shishya) learn under the close guidance of a master (guru).
 
• It emphasizes a holistic approach to learning, including discipline, devotion, and practice.
 
• It is widely followed in Indian classical music, dance, and other traditional art forms.
 
 
 
• **Bansuri**
 
 
• The bansuri is a traditional Indian bamboo flute associated with Lord Krishna in Indian mythology.
 
• It is a key instrument in Hindustani classical music and is known for its melodious and soulful sound.
 
• Hariprasad Chaurasia is credited with elevating the bansuri to the status of a major instrument in Indian classical music.
 
 
 
• **Indian Classical Music**
 
 
• Indian classical music is divided into two traditions: **Hindustani (North Indian) and Carnatic (South Indian)**.
 
• It is based on ragas (melodic frameworks) and talas (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Indian classical music has a rich history and is deeply intertwined with spirituality and cultural traditions.
